name: fmt
one_liner: A faster, safer way for C++ programs to turn numbers and data into readable text — the kind of plumbing almost every C++ application quietly relies on.
buyer: There isn't really a direct buyer — this is foundational open-source infrastructure that companies build on top of for free, not something anyone pays for on its own.
business_use_cases: A game studio's engine uses it internally to format debug logs and UI text faster than the C++ standard library allows.
A trading firm's low-latency C++ systems use it because it out-performs older formatting approaches, indirectly protecting their execution speed.
A tools vendor bundles it invisibly inside their C++ SDK so their own customers never know it's there.

money_ideas.idea: None realistic — this is a library companies consume for free; the only monetization path is sponsorship/donations to the maintainers.

steal_this: Not really a weekend business opportunity — at most, offer paid C++ performance-tuning consulting to teams that would benefit from adopting it.
